plan: 2 Chronicles 8:1-18; 1 Kings 9:15-28; 1 Kings 10:1-13; 2 Chronicles 9:1-12; 1 Kings 10:14-29; 2 Chronicles 9:13-28; 2 Chronicles 1:14-17

readings.title: Expanding the Terrestrial Footprint
readings.subtitle: Fortifications and the Architecture of Defense
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 8:1] And it came to be at the end of twenty years, that Shelomoh had built <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> his own house.
[2] As to the cities which Ḥuram had given to Shelomoh, Shelomoh had built them, and he settled the children of Yisra’ěl there.
[3] And Shelomoh went to Ḥamath Tsoḇah and took hold of it.
[4] And he built <dn>את</dn> Taḏmor in the wilderness, and <dn>את</dn> all the storage cities which he built in Ḥamath.
[5] And he built <dn>את</dn> Upper Běyth Ḥoron and <dn>את</dn> Lower Běyth Ḥoron, cities of defence, with walls, gates, and bars,
[6] also <dn>את</dn> Ba‛alath and <dn>את</dn> all the storage cities that Shelomoh had, and all the chariot cities and the cities of the cavalry, and all that Shelomoh desired to build in Yerushalayim, and in Leḇanon, and in all the land of his rule.

readings.title: The Labor Force Architecture
readings.subtitle: Subjecting the Remnant and Elevating the Sons of Yisra’ěl
readings.text:
[7] All the people who were left of the Ḥittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Ḥivvites, and the Yeḇusites, who were not of Yisra’ěl –
[8] their descendants who were left in the land after them, whom the children of Yisra’ěl did not destroy – from these Shelomoh raised compulsory labour, as it is to this day.
[9] And Shelomoh did not make slaves of the children of Yisra’ěl for his work, but they were men of battle, and chiefs of his officers, and commanders of his chariots, and his cavalry.
[10] And these were the chiefs of the officials of Sovereign Shelomoh: two hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people.

readings.title: Guarding the Set-Apart Reality
readings.subtitle: Relocating the Daughter of Mitsrayim
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 8:11] And Shelomoh brought <dn>את</dn> the daughter of Pharaoh up from the City of Daviḏ to the house he had built for her, for he said, “My wife does not dwell in the house of Daviḏ sovereign of Yisra’ěl, for the place where the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has come, is set-apart.”

readings.title: The Rhythms of Divine Order
readings.subtitle: Establishing the Appointed Times and Priestly Divisions
readings.text:
[12] Then Shelomoh offered ascending offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which he had built before the porch,
[13] even as the duty of every day required, offering according to the command of Mosheh, for the sabbaths, and for the new moons, and for the appointed times three times a year: the Festival of Matzot, and the Festival of Shaḇuʽoth, and the Festival of Sukkot.
[14] And according to the ruling of Daviḏ his father, he appointed <dn>את</dn> the divisions of the priests for their service, the Lěvites for their duties, to praise and serve before the priests, as the duty of each day required, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate, for so was the command of Daviḏ the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[15] And they did not turn aside from the command of the sovereign to the priests and Lěvites concerning any matter or concerning the treasuries.
[16] And all the work of Shelomoh was prepared from the day of the foundation of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> until it was completed. And the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was perfected.

readings.title: Maritime Expansion
readings.subtitle: The Fleet to Etsyon Geḇer and the Gold of Ophir
readings.text:
[17] Then Shelomoh went to Etsyon Geḇer and Ěyloth on the seacoast, in the land of Eḏom.
[18] And Ḥuram sent him ships by the hand of his servants, and servants who knew the sea. And they went with the servants of Shelomoh to Ophir, and took four hundred and fifty talents of gold from there, and brought it to Sovereign Shelomoh.

readings.title: The Architecture of Governance
readings.subtitle: The Compulsory Levy and Strategic Defense Cities
readings.text:
[1 Kings 9:15] And this is the purpose of the compulsory labour which Sovereign Shelomoh raised, to build <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> his own house, and <dn>את</dn> Millo, and <dn>את</dn> the wall of Yerushalayim, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥatsor, and <dn>את</dn> Meḡiddo, and <dn>את</dn> Gezer –
[16] Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim had gone up and taken <dn>את</dn> Gezer and burned it with fire, and had killed <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anites who dwelt in the city, and had given it as a payment for the bride to his daughter, Shelomoh’s wife –
[17] and Shelomoh built <dn>את</dn> Gezer, and <dn>את</dn> Lower Běyth Ḥoron,
[18] and <dn>את</dn> Ba‛alath, and <dn>את</dn> Tamar in the wilderness, in the land of Yehuḏah,
[19] and <dn>את</dn> all the storage cities that Shelomoh had, and <dn>את</dn> cities for his chariots and <dn>את</dn> cities for his cavalry, and <dn>את</dn> whatever Shelomoh desired to build in Yerushalayim, and in Leḇanon, and in all the land of his rule.

readings.title: The Social Hierarchy of the Kingdom
readings.subtitle: The Remnant Levy and the Status of Yisra’ěl
readings.text:
[20] All the people who were left of the Amorites, the Ḥittites, the Perizzites, the Ḥivvites, and the Yeḇusites, who were not of the children of Yisra’ěl –
[21] their descendants who were left in the land after them, whom the children of Yisra’ěl had not been able to destroy completely – from these Shelomoh raised compulsory labour, as it is to this day.
[22] But Shelomoh did not make slaves of the children of Yisra’ěl, because they were men of battle, and his servants, and his rulers, and his officers, and commanders of his chariots, and his cavalry.
[23] These were the chiefs of the officials who were over the work of Shelomoh: five hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people who did the work.

readings.title: Structural Completion
readings.subtitle: The Millo and the Cycle of Ascending Offerings
readings.text:
[24] But the daughter of Pharaoh came up from the City of Daviḏ to her house that he built for her. Then he built <dn>את</dn> Millo.
[25] And three times a year Shelomoh brought ascending offerings and peace offerings on the slaughter-place which he had built for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he burned incense with that which was before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – thus gave completeness to <dn>את</dn> the House.

readings.title: The Naval Expeditions
readings.subtitle: Harvesting the Wealth of Ophir
readings.text:
[26] And Sovereign Shelomoh built a fleet of ships at Etsyon Geḇer, which is near Ěyloth on the shore of the Sea of Reeds, in the land of Eḏom.
[27] And Ḥiram sent <dn>את</dn> his servants with the fleet, seamen who knew the sea, to work with the servants of Shelomoh.
[28] And they went to Ophir, and took four hundred and twenty talents of gold from there, and brought it to Sovereign Shelomoh.

readings.title: The Verification of Wisdom
readings.subtitle: The Sovereigness of Sheḇa Witnesses the Terrestrial Order
readings.text:
[1 Kings 10:1] And the sovereigness of Sheḇa heard of <dn>את</dn> the report of Shelomoh concerning the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and came to try him with hard questions.
[2] And she came to Yerushalayim with a very great company, with camels that bore spices, very much gold, and precious stones. And she came to Shelomoh, and she spoke with him about all that was in her heart.
[3] And Shelomoh answered <dn>את</dn> all her questions. There was no matter hidden for the sovereign that he did not make known to her.
[4] And the sovereigness of Sheḇa saw <dn>את</dn> all the wisdom of Shelomoh, and the house that he had built,
[5] and the food on his table, and the seating of his servants, and the service of his waiters and their attire, and his cupbearers, and his ascending offerings which he offered in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and there was no more spirit in her.
[6] Then she said to the sovereign, “The word I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom was true.
[7] “But I did not believe the words until I came and saw with my own eyes. And see, I have not been told the half! Your wisdom and prosperity exceed the report which I heard.
[8] “Blessed are your men and blessed are these your servants, who stand continually before you, who are hearing your wisdom!
[9] “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who delighted in you, to put you on the throne of Yisra’ěl! Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has loved Yisra’ěl forever, therefore <dn>He</dn> made you sovereign, to do right-ruling and righteousness.”
[10] And she gave the sovereign one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and very many spices, and precious stones. Never again did so many spices come as the sovereigness of Sheḇa gave to Sovereign Shelomoh.

readings.title: Materials for the House
readings.subtitle: The Import and Application of Almug Wood
readings.text:
[11] And also, the ships of Ḥiram, which brought gold from Ophir, brought almug wood, a great many, and precious stones from Ophir.
[12] And the sovereign made <dn>את</dn> steps of the almug wood for the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and for the sovereign’s house, also lyres and harps for singers. No such almug wood has come or been seen to this day.

readings.title: The Exchange of Generosity
readings.subtitle: The Departure of the Sovereigness
readings.text: [13] And Sovereign Shelomoh gave the sovereigness of Sheḇa <dn>את</dn> all she desired, whatever she asked, besides what he gave her according to the hand of Sovereign Shelomoh. And she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.

readings.title: Testing the Divine Architecture
readings.subtitle: The Sovereigness of Sheḇa and the Reflection of YeHoVaH's Order
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 9:1] And the sovereigness of Sheḇa heard of <dn>את</dn> the report of Shelomoh, and came to Yerushalayim to try Shelomoh with hard questions, with a very great company, and camels bearing spices, and much gold, and precious stones. And she came to Shelomoh, and she spoke with him about all that was in her heart.
[2] And Shelomoh answered <dn>את</dn> all her questions. And there was no matter hidden for Shelomoh which he did not make known to her.
[3] And the sovereigness of Sheḇa saw <dn>את</dn> the wisdom of Shelomoh, and the house that he had built,
[4] and the food on his table, and the seating of his servants, and the service of his waiters and their attire, and his cupbearers and their attire, and his ascending offerings that he offered up in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and there was no more spirit in her.
[5] Then she said to the sovereign, “True was the word I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom.
[6] “But I did not believe their words until I came and saw with my own eyes. And see, I have not been told the half of the greatness of your wisdom! You exceed the report which I heard.
[7] “Blessed are your men and blessed are these your servants, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
[8] “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who delighted in you, to put you on <dn>His</dn> throne to be sovereign for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>! Because your <dn>Elohim</dn> has loved Yisra’ěl, to establish them forever, therefore <dn>He</dn> made you sovereign over them, to do right-ruling and righteousness.”
[9] And she gave the sovereign one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and very many spices, and precious stones. And there has not been any spices such as those the sovereigness of Sheḇa gave to Sovereign Shelomoh.

readings.title: The Algum Wood Allocation
readings.subtitle: Stairs and Instruments for the House of YeHoVaH
readings.text:
[10] And also, the servants of Ḥuram and the servants of Shelomoh, who brought gold from Ophir, brought algum wood and precious stones.
[11] And the sovereign made <dn>את</dn> stairs of the algum wood for the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and for the sovereign’s house, also lyres and harps for singers. And there was never seen the like of them before in the land of Yehuḏah.

readings.title: The Completion of the Visit
readings.subtitle: A Sovereign's Bounty
readings.text: [12] And Sovereign Shelomoh gave to the sovereigness of Sheḇa <dn>את</dn> all she desired, whatever she asked, besides that which she had brought to the sovereign. And she turned and went to her own land, she and her servants.

readings.title: The Number of Ultimate Authority
readings.subtitle: The 666 Talents of Gold and the Warning of Decline
readings.text:
[1 Kings 10:14] And the weight of gold that came to Shelomoh yearly was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
[15] besides that from men of travel, and the profit from traders, and from all the sovereigns of Araḇia, and from the governors of the land.

readings.title: The Symbols of Unprecedented Authority
readings.subtitle: The Golden Shields and the Great Ivory Throne
readings.text:
[16] And Sovereign Shelomoh made two hundred large shields of beaten gold – six hundred pieces of gold went into each shield;
[17] and three hundred shields of beaten gold – three minas of gold went into each shield. And the sovereign put them in the House of the Forest of Leḇanon.
[18] And the sovereign made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with refined gold.
[19] The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was round at the back, and there were armrests on either side of the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the armrests.
[20] And twelve lions were standing there, one on each side of the six steps. The like of it was never made in any reign.
[21] And all the drinking vessels of Sovereign Shelomoh were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Leḇanon were of refined gold – not of silver, for this was reckoned of little value in the days of Shelomoh.

readings.title: Global Homage
readings.subtitle: The Fleet of Tarshish and the Influx of Tribute
readings.text:
[22] For the sovereign had ships of Tarshish at sea with the fleet of Ḥiram. Once every three years the ships of Tarshish came bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and baboons.
[23] And Sovereign Shelomoh was greater than any of the sovereigns of the earth in riches and wisdom.
[24] And all the earth sought <dn>את</dn> the presence of Shelomoh to hear his wisdom, which <dn>Elohim</dn> had put in his heart.
[25] And they were each bringing <dn>את</dn> his present: objects of silver and objects of gold, and garments, and armour, and spices, horses, and mules, the matter of a year by year.

readings.title: The Seeds of Compromise
readings.subtitle: Returning to Mitsrayim, the Crucible of Burdens, for Military Might
readings.text:
[26] And Shelomoh gathered chariots and horsemen, and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the sovereign in Yerushalayim.
[27] And the sovereign made <dn>את</dn> silver as common in Yerushalayim as stones, and he made <dn>את</dn> cedars as plenty as the sycamores which are in the low country.
[28] And Shelomoh had horses brought out from Mitsrayim and Quěh; the sovereign’s merchants bought them in Quěh at a price.
[29] And a chariot came up and went out from Mitsrayim for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse one hundred and fifty. And so, by their hand, they brought them out to all the sovereigns of the Ḥittites and the sovereigns of Aram.

readings.title: The Zenith of Economic Power
readings.subtitle: The Annual Revenue of 666 Talents
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 9:13] And the weight of gold that came to Shelomoh yearly was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
[14] besides that which the merchants and traders brought. And all the sovereigns of Araḇia and governors of the land were bringing gold and silver to Shelomoh.

readings.title: The Throne of Splendor
readings.subtitle: Golden Shields and Vessels of the Forest
readings.text:
[15] And Sovereign Shelomoh made two hundred large shields of beaten gold – six hundred pieces of beaten gold went into each shield,
[16] and three hundred shields of beaten gold – three hundred pieces of gold went into each shield. And the sovereign put them in the House of the Forest of Leḇanon.
[17] And the sovereign made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with clean gold,
[18] and six steps led to the throne, with a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the throne; and there were armrests on either side of the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the armrests.
[19] And twelve lions were standing there, one on each side of the six steps. The like of it was not in any reign.
[20] And all the drinking vessels of Sovereign Shelomoh were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Leḇanon were of refined gold – silver was reckoned of little value in the days of Shelomoh.
[21] For the sovereign’s ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Ḥuram. Once in three years the ships of Tarshish came, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, apes, and baboons.

readings.title: The Center of the Earth
readings.subtitle: Sovereigns Seek the Wisdom Given by Elohim
readings.text:
[22] And Sovereign Shelomoh became greater than all the sovereigns of the earth in riches and wisdom.
[23] And all the sovereigns of the earth sought <dn>את</dn> the presence of Shelomoh to hear his wisdom, which <dn>Elohim</dn> had put in his heart.
[24] And each man brought <dn>את</dn> his present: objects of silver, and objects of gold, and garments, and armour, and spices, horses and mules, the matter of a year by year.

readings.title: Military Expansion and Economic Dominance
readings.subtitle: Chariots and Horses from the Land of Mitsrayim
readings.text:
[25] And Shelomoh had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the sovereign at Yerushalayim.
[26] And he ruled over all the sovereigns from the River to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Mitsrayim.
[27] And the sovereign made <dn>את</dn> silver in Yerushalayim as the stones, and he made <dn>את</dn> cedar trees as plenty as the sycamores which are in the low country.
[28] And they were bringing horses to Shelomoh from Mitsrayim and from all lands.

readings.title: The Paradox of Prosperity
readings.subtitle: Silver as Stones and the Return to Mitsrayim for Might
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 1:14] And Shelomoh gathered chariots and horsemen, and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the sovereign in Yerushalayim.
[15] And the sovereign made <dn>את</dn> silver and <dn>את</dn> gold to be as stones in Yerushalayim, and he made <dn>את</dn> cedars to be as plenty as the sycamores which are in the low country.
[16] And Shelomoh had horses imported from Mitsrayim and from Quě – the sovereign’s merchants bought them in Quě at a price.
[17] And they came up and brought from Mitsrayim a chariot for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for one hundred and fifty. And so, for all the sovereigns of the Ḥittites and the sovereigns of Aram, they brought them out by their hand.
